title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Security
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of dependency and supply-chain security in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply dependency and supply-chain security to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: Dependency and Supply-Chain Security is lesson 183 in Security, Reliability, and Production Practices. Production code must treat inputs and dependencies as untrusted, make failure behavior explicit, protect sensitive information, and provide repeatable verification and release steps.
content.why_it_matters: Production quality includes safe failure behavior, observable operation, and a repeatable way to ship updates. This lesson focuses on dependency and supply-chain security and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Production code must treat inputs and dependencies as untrusted, make failure behavior explicit, protect sensitive information, and provide repeatable verification and release steps.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to learn it
content_blocks.text: Start with the smallest valid case for dependency and supply-chain security. Predict the output, run or inspect the example in the stated toolchain, then change one input or rule and compare the result. For production code, record assumptions and verify boundary cases.

items.title: Dependency risks
items.text: Compose small collaborators when behavior varies independently; inject dependencies at a clear composition boundary.

items.title: Package version management
items.text: Keep dependencies and project settings reproducible, and inspect changes before committing or releasing.

items.title: Vulnerability advisories
items.text: For vulnerability advisories, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to dependency and supply-chain security, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Reviewing third-party libraries
items.text: For reviewing third-party libraries, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to dependency and supply-chain security, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Protecting build pipelines
items.text: For protecting build pipelines, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to dependency and supply-chain security, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Managing secrets outside source code
items.text: Define trust boundaries, store secrets outside source, fail safely, and verify the release artifact in the target environment.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates dependency and supply-chain security. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates dependency and supply-chain security rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for dependency and supply-chain security before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.
content.expected_output: Review package source, versions, advisories, and lockfile changes.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
